name: Mombasa-Nairobi Standard Gauge Railway
value: $3.2bn; 2014 loans of $1.6bn concessional and $1.63bn commercial
backer: China Exim Bank (about 90%); China Road and Bridge Corp built and operated it
china_gets: Building and operating contracts for a Chinese state firm; Libor+3.6% on the commercial loan; a 15-year take-or-pay cargo guarantee
host_case: Kenya's biggest project since independence; Ruto published the loan documents in 2022

name: Addis Ababa-Djibouti Railway
value: About $4bn; Ethiopia's $2.49bn China Exim loan was restructured in 2018 and now matures in 2044
backer: China Exim Bank; CREC and CCECC built it
china_gets: Building contracts for CREC, CCECC and NORINCO; Libor+3% interest; a supply corridor to Djibouti's ports, where China Merchants owns a stake
host_case: Ethiopia's main route to the sea

name: Port de Djibouti / Doraleh stake
value: China Merchants bought 23.5% of Port de Djibouti S.A. for $185m in 2012-13
backer: China Merchants Port Holdings
china_gets: A share in Djibouti's port operator, on the Bab el-Mandeb strait
host_case: Djibouti presents itself as a neutral hub that hosts many countries' bases

name: PLA support base, Djibouti
value: Opened 1 Aug 2017; lease reported at about $20m a year
backer: People's Liberation Army Navy
china_gets: China's first overseas base; about 400 PLA marines and a pier for large warships (US DoD, cited by CRS)
host_case: Beijing calls it a support facility for anti-piracy and evacuation missions

name: Lamu Port (LAPSSET)
value: First 3 berths; berth 1 opened 20 May 2021
backer: Built by China Communications Construction Co; funded by Kenya
china_gets: A building contract for CCCC; no Chinese ownership stake found
host_case: Kenya's gateway to South Sudan and Ethiopia

name: Bagamoyo Port
value: $10bn plan agreed in 2013 with China Merchants and Oman; suspended in 2019; the Chinese partner pulled out in 2022
backer: Formerly China Merchants; now an MoU with AGL (MSC), signed Dec 2025
china_gets: Nothing; the talks collapsed
host_case: Tanzania's ports authority rejected the terms: tax exemptions and the investors' freedom to set port charges

name: Sicomines copper-cobalt (minerals for infrastructure)
value: Up to $7bn of infrastructure under the revised 2024 deal
backer: Sinohydro and China Railway Group
china_gets: Copper and cobalt output in exchange for infrastructure
host_case: Kinshasa renegotiated the deal for more infrastructure

name: Chinese loans to Africa, 2000-2024
value: $180.87bn in 1,319 loan commitments from 42 lenders (amounts committed, not paid out)
backer: China Exim Bank, China Development Bank and others
china_gets: Interest; contracts for Chinese firms; repayment in resources in some deals
host_case: Governments say they borrowed to fill gaps Western lenders left

name: Top Chinese borrowers in Africa, 2000-2023
value: Angola $46.05bn cumulative; ranking after it: Ethiopia, Egypt, Nigeria, Kenya, Zambia, South Africa, Sudan, Ghana, Cameroon (dollar figures for those not in the brief)
backer: China Exim Bank, China Development Bank
china_gets: Oil-backed repayment in Angola's case; contracts for Chinese firms
host_case: Angola negotiated debt relief in 2024 rather than restructuring

name: Lekki Deep Sea Port
value: Opened 23 Jan 2023
backer: China Harbour Engineering (CHEC) built it; China Development Bank financed
china_gets: CHEC 52.5% stake (Tolaram 22.5%, Lagos 20%, NPA 5%)
host_case: Lagos calls it Nigeria's first deep-sea port

name: Dar es Salaam port upgrade
value: World Bank-financed berths 1-7, RoRo, channel works
backer: China Harbour Engineering (contractor); World Bank financing
china_gets: Construction contracts only; operators are DP World (berths 4-7) and Adani (CT2)
host_case: Dar es Salaam chose Gulf and Indian operators

name: Kribi deep-water port
value: Container terminal run by KCT consortium
backer: China Harbour Engineering built it; CHEC is a KCT shareholder with CMA CGM and Bollore
china_gets: Shareholding in the terminal operator (exact % not confirmed in a filing)
host_case: Cameroon's main deep-water port

name: Husab and Rossing uranium
value: Husab 5,318 t U3O8 (2023); Rossing 68.62% CNUC
backer: CGN and China-Africa Development Fund (Taurus Minerals, 90% of Swakop Uranium); CNNC's CNUC at Rossing
china_gets: Uranium supply; Namibia's state Epangelo holds 10% of Husab
host_case: Namibia keeps a state stake and royalty

name: Arcadia and Bikita lithium
value: Huayou paid $422m for 100% of Arcadia (completed Apr 2022); Sinomine paid $180m for 74% of Bikita
backer: Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt; Sinomine Resource
china_gets: Lithium concentrate for Chinese battery supply chains
host_case: Zimbabwe banned raw lithium ore exports in Dec 2022 to force local processing

name: Gwadar Port (CPEC)
value: 40-year concession held by China Overseas Port Holding Co since 2013
backer: China Overseas Port Holding Co (COPHC)
china_gets: 91% of gross port revenue and 85% of free-zone revenue for 40 years (minister to Senate); an Arabian Sea port near Hormuz
host_case: Pakistan says the port is CPEC's flagship gateway and will return to the Gwadar Port Authority at the end of the concession
confidence_reason: Revenue split stated by Pakistan's minister in the Senate and reported by Dawn

name: CPEC power plants (Chinese IPPs)
value: $15.36bn of outstanding Chinese IPP debt across 21 projects (May 2024); Rs423bn of unpaid dues to Chinese plants (2025); AidData puts the energy portfolio at nearly $20bn
backer: Chinese state-owned and private power companies; Chinese banks
china_gets: Dollar-indexed, government-guaranteed returns on equity; building contracts; debt service
host_case: Pakistan says the plants ended its blackouts and is now trying to stretch out the debt and cut payments
confidence_reason: Figures come from Pakistani press and AidData and cover the whole portfolio; point is the country centroid

name: Hambantota Port
value: $1.12bn deal (2017): $973.66m for 85% of HIPG; 99-year lease
backer: China Merchants Port Holdings; port originally built with Chinese loans
china_gets: Majority control of the port operator for 99 years; a 15-year ban on competing ports within 100 km
host_case: Sri Lanka used the proceeds to ease its debt and kept security oversight; the deal was signed despite opposition objections
confidence_reason: Terms appear in a primary HKEX filing and Reuters reporting

name: Colombo Port City
value: About $1.4bn of CHEC investment; 116 ha of reclaimed land on a 99-year lease
backer: CHEC Port City Colombo (a CCCC subsidiary)
china_gets: Leasehold rights over 116 ha of new land next to the CBD, which it can sublease
host_case: Sri Lanka passed the 2021 Port City Economic Commission Act to create a special financial zone
confidence_reason: Figures come from secondary sources (ISAS NUS, Daily Mirror); the investor's own FAQ confirms the lease structure

name: Padma Bridge Rail Link
value: $2.67bn China Exim preferential buyer's credit (2018) covering 85% of a $3.13bn contract; 2% interest, 20-year term
backer: China Exim Bank; China Railway Group (CREC) built it
china_gets: A large building contract for CREC; interest
host_case: Bangladesh says it is a key link between Dhaka and the southwest
confidence_reason: Loan recorded by AidData and Bangladeshi press

name: Pokhara International Airport
value: China Exim concessional loan of RMB 1.02bn (about $216m), 2% interest
backer: China Exim Bank; China CAMC Engineering
china_gets: Building contract for CAMC; interest
host_case: Nepal asked China to turn the loan into a grant; its anti-graft body charged CAMC and Nepali officials with inflating costs (2025)
confidence_reason: AidData record plus Kathmandu Post and NYT reporting

name: China-Maldives Friendship (Sinamale) Bridge
value: China Exim concessional loan of RMB 455.6m; the bridge cost about $200m
backer: China Exim Bank; CCCC
china_gets: Interest; building contract; influence in Malé
host_case: The 2018 government vowed to renegotiate Chinese debt; Reuters estimated Chinese-linked liabilities at about $1.5bn in 2018
confidence_reason: Loan is documented, but estimates of total Maldives debt to China vary widely

name: Kyaukphyu Deep Sea Port and SEZ
value: Phase 1 cut to $1.3bn in the 2018 framework agreement (from a $7.2bn plan); CITIC holds 70%
backer: CITIC-led consortium
china_gets: Control of a Bay of Bengal port and the pipeline terminus, bypassing Malacca
host_case: Myanmar negotiated CITIC's share down from 85% to 70% and shrank phase 1 over debt-trap fears; the port sits in a conflict zone
confidence_reason: Deal terms are well sourced, but construction status since 2021 is unclear

name: Myanmar-China oil and gas pipelines
value: Oil line design capacity is 22m tonnes a year; gas line 12 bcm a year
backer: CNPC (50.9% of the oil line) with MOGE
china_gets: An energy import route from the Indian Ocean to Yunnan that bypasses Malacca
host_case: Myanmar receives transit fees and gas offtake
confidence_reason: Sourced to a BRI Monitor case study; coordinates mark the Kyaukphyu/Made Island terminus

name: Laos-China Railway (Vientiane-Boten)
value: About $5.9-6bn line; China holds 70% of the JV; about 60% debt-financed
backer: Chinese state firms (JV); Chinese lenders
china_gets: Rail link from Kunming toward Thailand and Singapore; JV control
host_case: Laos calls it the way to turn a landlocked country into a land-linked one; economists warn about debt
confidence_reason: Reuters and AP

name: Ream Naval Base expansion
value: China funded a 300m deep-water pier, a 5,000-ton dry dock and a joint logistics and training centre (opened Apr 2025)
backer: Chinese government (PLA)
china_gets: PLAN corvettes have berthed continuously at the main pier since Dec 2023 (AMTI); joint training centre on the Gulf of Thailand
host_case: Cambodia says the base is open to all friendly navies; a US warship docked there in 2026
confidence_reason: Construction and use are documented, but whether China has exclusive access is contested

name: Dara Sakor (UDG) development
value: 99-year land lease (2008)
backer: Tianjin Union Development Group (UDG)
china_gets: Coastal land and a long runway that the US says could host military assets
host_case: Cambodia calls it a tourism project; the US sanctioned UDG in 2020 over evictions and corruption
confidence_reason: The military use claim is US government allegation and analysts dispute it; the sanction itself is documented

name: Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Railway (Whoosh)
value: $7.3bn including a $1.2bn overrun; 75% financed by China Development Bank (2% on USD, 3.46% on CNY); restructuring talks in 2025
backer: China Development Bank; Chinese consortium holds 40% of KCIC
china_gets: Interest; equity in the operator
host_case: Prabowo pledged state support; Indonesian SOEs are absorbing the losses; the anti-graft agency (KPK) is investigating possible mark-ups
confidence_reason: Straits Times and The Diplomat

name: Indonesia Morowali Industrial Park (IMIP)
value: CDB loans for the park's power stations include $384m for phase 1 and a $559-574m share of a syndicated loan for phase 3
backer: Tsingshan Group with Bintang Delapan; China Development Bank
china_gets: Nickel supply for stainless steel and EV batteries; operating control
host_case: Indonesia's nickel export ban was meant to force processing onshore
confidence_reason: AidData records plus the park's own site

name: East Coast Rail Link (ECRL)
value: Construction cost RM50.27bn; RM74.96bn including development costs
backer: China Communications Construction Co (CCCC)
china_gets: Building contract; a land bridge that offers a Malacca alternative
host_case: Malaysia renegotiated the cost down in 2019; the line is due to open Jan 2027
confidence_reason: Malaysian transport ministry figures reported by The Edge

name: Thai-Chinese HSR (Bangkok-Nakhon Ratchasima)
value: 179.412bn baht for phase 1; Thailand pays for construction
backer: Thailand funds it; China supplies technical systems
china_gets: Technical systems contracts; a link to the Laos-China railway
host_case: Thailand chose to self-finance; the project is behind schedule, with service targeted for 2030
confidence_reason: Thai project site and Reuters; no Chinese loan

name: Cat Linh-Ha Dong Metro, Hanoi
value: Cost rose 57% to $868m; China Exim loans of about $670m
backer: China Exim Bank
china_gets: Interest; building contract
host_case: Vietnam criticised delays and overruns; auditors flagged improper costs
confidence_reason: AidData record plus Vietnamese press

name: New Centennial Water Source-Kaliwa Dam
value: $211.2m China Exim preferential buyer's credit (2018); 2% interest, 20-year term
backer: China Exim Bank
china_gets: Interest; building contract
host_case: Manila says the dam is needed for its water supply
confidence_reason: Loan agreement published by the Philippine Department of Finance

name: Chancay Port
value: $1.3bn first phase; COSCO bought 60% of Terminales Portuarios Chancay for $225m in 2019
backer: COSCO Shipping Ports (60%); Volcan (40%)
china_gets: Majority control of a deep-water Pacific hub with 1m TEU capacity and direct Shanghai routes; the terminal owns its land, so no concession is needed
host_case: Peru says Chancay will make it a regional trade hub and cut shipping time to China by 12 days; US officials have raised possible military use
confidence_reason: Stake and price in COSCO's own exchange filing; cost and inauguration confirmed by Peru's state news agency and Reuters

name: Espacio Lejano deep-space station (Neuquén)
value: 200-hectare site on a 50-year tax-free lease; China funded about $54.5m of construction (House Select Committee figure)
backer: China Satellite Launch and Tracking Control General (CLTC, PLA-linked); China Harbour Engineering built it
china_gets: A 35m deep-space antenna in the southern hemisphere for tracking, command and data, run under Chinese labour law with no effective Argentine inspection
host_case: Argentina says the station is civilian (a 2016 addendum says so) and compares it to the ESA station in Mendoza
confidence_reason: The lease and PLA-linked operator are well documented; military use is alleged, not proven

name: Coca Codo Sinclair hydroelectric plant
value: $1.98bn EPC contract; $1.68bn China Exim loan at 6.9% (85% of cost); Ecuador's comptroller found 7,648 cracks
backer: China Exim Bank; Sinohydro (PowerChina) built it
china_gets: The building contract, a 6.9% fixed-rate loan insured by Sinosure; in the 2025 settlement PowerChina takes over operation
host_case: Ecuador's largest power plant (1,500 MW); Ecuador went to ICC arbitration over defects, then in 2025 agreed to drop it
confidence_reason: Loan terms from AidData's project record; defects from Ecuador's Contraloría; settlement reported by Reuters

name: CDB oil-backed loans and PetroChina prepayments
value: Several CDB facilities, e.g. $2.05bn (2011, repaid early in 2018) and $2.03bn (2016); PetroChina $1bn oil prepayment
backer: China Development Bank; PetroChina / Unipec
china_gets: Repayment from Petroecuador oil sales routed into CDB-controlled accounts with minimum balances; long-term crude supply
host_case: Ecuador says the loans financed infrastructure and has prepaid or rescheduled them, with maturities extended to 2027
confidence_reason: Loan facilities and repayment mechanics documented in AidData project records

name: Joint China-Venezuela Fund (oil-for-loans)
value: $60bn+ CDB commitments via the Joint Fund since 2007; AidData counts $105.6bn of Chinese loan commitments 2000-2018; $10-15bn estimated outstanding (2026)
backer: China Development Bank; CNPC/ChinaOil buys the oil
china_gets: Oil cargoes for debt service, paid into a CDB collection account with set-off rights
host_case: Venezuela defaulted in 2017; China granted grace periods; US control of exports in 2026 caught cargoes that had been servicing Chinese debt
confidence_reason: Structure and totals from AidData; current outstanding range from Reuters citing SocGen and JPMorgan (estimates differ)

name: Uyuni lithium plants (YLB-CBC)
value: $1.03bn contract for two direct-extraction plants, 35,000 t/yr lithium carbonate
backer: Hong Kong CBC consortium (includes CATL); state YLB holds 51%
china_gets: Building and operating rights at the world's largest lithium resource, at CBC's own cost and risk
host_case: Bolivia's government backs the deal; a court suspended its passage in 2025 pending environmental studies and indigenous consultation
confidence_reason: Contract signed and reported by Reuters and Bolivia's energy ministry, but not ratified and no plant is operating

name: Tianqi stake in SQM (Salar de Atacama)
value: About 22% of SQM held by Tianqi Lithium
backer: Tianqi Lithium
china_gets: A large minority stake in the world's second-biggest lithium producer and a share of its Atacama brine output
host_case: Chile put Atacama lithium under a Codelco-SQM partnership; Tianqi's legal challenge was rejected by the Supreme Court in January 2026
confidence_reason: Stake and the court ruling reported by Chile's state defence council and Caixin

name: Cauchari-Olaroz lithium
value: 40,000 t/yr lithium carbonate; production began June 2023
backer: Ganfeng Lithium (with Lithium Argentina and Jujuy's JEMSE)
china_gets: Lithium carbonate supply for Chinese battery makers
host_case: Jujuy province is a partner through JEMSE and backs lithium output as a source of revenue
confidence_reason: Start-up reported by market and Chinese business press; ownership shares not set out in these sources

name: Mariana lithium
value: 20,000 t/yr lithium chloride first phase; production began February 2025
backer: Ganfeng Lithium
china_gets: Lithium chloride feedstock for Ganfeng's refineries
host_case: Salta province promotes the project as investment and jobs
confidence_reason: Start-up in Ganfeng's exchange filing and Reuters; no investment figure in these sources

name: Tres Quebradas (3Q) lithium
value: 20,000 t/yr lithium carbonate first phase; production began September 2025
backer: Zijin Mining
china_gets: Lithium carbonate supply
host_case: Catamarca province backs the project as investment
confidence_reason: Start-up reported only by the company; site could not be reached for verification

name: Néstor Kirchner and Jorge Cepernic dams (Santa Cruz)
value: $4.71bn syndicated loan (CDB $2.49bn, ICBC, Bank of China), signed 2014; works largely stalled since 2023
backer: China Development Bank, ICBC, Bank of China; Gezhouba-led consortium builds
china_gets: The building contract and loan repayment; the deal was tied to the wider China-Argentina strategic partnership
host_case: Argentina says the 1,310 MW dams are needed for power; successive governments renegotiated and delayed them
confidence_reason: Loan in AidData's record and Argentina's Boletín Oficial; stalled status from Argentine press

name: Belgrano Cargas freight railway rehabilitation
value: $2.47bn CMEC contract (2010); $2.1bn CDB/ICBC buyer's credit (2012) covering 85%
backer: China Development Bank, ICBC; China Machinery Engineering Corp (CMEC)
china_gets: The rehabilitation contract, Chinese rolling stock and rail supplies, and a freight route for northern grain to the ports
host_case: Argentina says the line cuts the cost of moving grain from the north to the river ports
confidence_reason: Contract and loan documented in AidData and Argentina's official contract text

name: China-Argentina currency swap
value: $18bn swap line; the activated CNY35bn (about $5bn) tranche was renewed in April 2025
backer: People's Bank of China
china_gets: Wider use of the yuan in Argentina's reserves and trade and political leverage over a reserve-poor central bank
host_case: Argentina's central bank says the swap supports its reserves; the US has urged Argentina to end it
confidence_reason: Central bank statement and Reuters

name: TCP container terminal, Paranaguá
value: R$2.9bn (about $924m) for 90% of TCP; deal closed February 2018
backer: China Merchants Port Holdings
china_gets: Control of Brazil's third-largest container terminal, a main outlet for grain and meat exports
host_case: Brazil's transport ministry welcomed the investment
confidence_reason: Price and stake in CMPort's exchange filing and Brazil's transport ministry

name: State Grid Brazil: Belo Monte lines and CPFL Energia
value: Two ±800 kV Belo Monte UHV lines (won 2014 and 2015); 54.6% of CPFL Energia bought in 2017, later about 84%
backer: State Grid Corporation of China (State Grid Brazil Holding)
china_gets: Ownership of long-distance transmission and Brazil's largest private distributor; a showcase for Chinese UHV technology
host_case: Brazil awarded the lines at public auction and approved the CPFL purchase
confidence_reason: Auctions from Brazil's mines and energy ministry; history from State Grid Brazil

name: CNOOC stake in the Stabroek Block
value: 25% working interest (ExxonMobil 45% operator; Hess/Chevron 30%); the block passed 500m barrels produced in 2024
backer: CNOOC
china_gets: A quarter of the consortium's oil from one of the world's fastest-growing fields
host_case: Guyana says its share of the oil is rising as cost recovery falls
confidence_reason: Ownership shares widely reported, including by Guyana's own information department

name: Bogotá Metro Line 1
value: COP13.83 trillion concession (about $3.55bn, Reuters); 23.96km elevated line, 16 stations
backer: China Harbour Engineering (85%) and Xi'an Rail Transportation Group (15%) as Metro Línea 1
china_gets: A 28-year concession to build, supply trains for and run the line for 20 years
host_case: Colombia's government and Bogotá signed it as the city's first metro
confidence_reason: Concession terms from Colombia's transport ministry and Bogotá city hall

name: Mirador copper mine
value: $329m CDB-backed loan to buy Corriente Resources (2010); $1.29bn syndicated loan for mine development (2014); exports began 2019
backer: CRCC-Tongguan (China Railway Construction Corp and Tongling Nonferrous) via EcuaCorriente; China Development Bank
china_gets: Ecuador's first large-scale copper mine and its concentrate
host_case: Ecuador's government signed an addendum to expand output; local and indigenous groups contest its impact
confidence_reason: Loans in AidData records; first exports reported by Reuters

name: Las Bambas copper mine
value: $5.85bn purchase from Glencore (2014) by an MMG-led Chinese consortium; MMG announced a $2bn investment in 2022
backer: MMG (China Minmetals), Guoxin, CITIC
china_gets: One of the world's biggest copper mines and its concentrate
host_case: Peru counts on the mine for revenue; communities have blocked the mining road repeatedly over land and compensation
confidence_reason: Price from CITIC; conflicts and investment reported by Reuters
